record.one_liner: Team messaging and collaboration platform with a developer platform (Web API, apps, and an official MCP server).
record.auth_notes: critic: added api_key. Apps are installed via the v2 OAuth 2.0 flow, and bot tokens (xoxb-) are also obtained by installing an app from its settings page (copied from the dashboard). User-facing MCP also uses OAuth.
record.access_notes: critic: confirmed self_serve_free. Anyone can create a Slack app and install it in a workspace; free developer sandboxes exist; unlisted distribution to other workspaces needs no Slack review.
record.api_notes: Web API is HTTP RPC-style methods at slack.com/api/METHOD_FAMILY.method, described by Slack as not strictly REST. Mapped to rest as the closest enum value.
record.blocker_notes: critic: verdict ready_with_review -> ready, blocker app_review -> none. Unlisted distributed apps work without review; the Marketplace is recommended only for commercial distribution, not required. Caveat: the official MCP server is limited to Marketplace and internal apps.

evidence.quote: Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.
Bot token strings begin with xoxb-.
Sandboxes are Enterprise environments that you can use to build against all of Slack’s features safely and securely at no cost.
While it's not a REST API, those familiar with REST should be at home with its foundations in HTTP.
The Slack MCP server provides AI agents with secure access to your Slack workspace or Enterprise organisation
Only apps published in the Slack Marketplace and internal apps can use MCP at this time; unlisted apps are prohibited from using MCP.
Distributing your unlisted app is perfect for when you want to test out your app by running a pilot for early customers
